strategy.summary: The todo app (public/app.js, in-memory state per page load) lets users tick/untick todos, filter All/Active/Completed (aria-pressed buttons) and clear completed todos. The tests drive the real UI and real static server in Chromium and prove the strike-through and count change, the filter contents and pressed state, and the visibility and effect of "Clear completed".
inScope: Completing/uncompleting a todo via its checkbox (strike-through, items-left count)
All / Active / Completed filters: list contents and aria-pressed state
Clear completed: visibility and removal of completed todos
outOfScope: Persistence across reloads (app keeps todos in memory only; the ticket doesn't ask for it)
assumptions: Nothing is faked: server.js only serves static files and runs for real via Playwright's existing webServer config; all todo state lives in page memory, so each test starts from an empty list in its own page and needs no cleanup.
None of these actions can be refused by the app (no validation on tick, filter or clear), so the negative case is that 'Clear completed' stays hidden when nothing is completed (TC6).
"Struck through" is checked as the computed style text-decoration-line: line-through on the todo's title span (styles.css: li.completed span), which is what the user sees.
Todos are created through the UI (label 'What needs doing?' + Add), as the existing spec does; locators use roles and exact accessible names.
openQuestions: The existing playwright.config.js webServer uses port 4173, the same as `npm start`, with reuseExistingServer outside CI; TestForge's runner fixes BASE_URL to that port, so the tests keep it. Moving the test server to its own port is a follow-up.

risks.description: Count text or strike-through not updated on untick (state reversal bug)
risks.mitigation: TC2 ticks then unticks and asserts both strike-through removed and count restored

risks.description: Filters showing wrong todos or pressed state not following the selection
risks.mitigation: TC3-TC5 use a mix of completed and active todos and assert exact list contents and aria-pressed on all three buttons

risks.description: Clear completed removing only one todo, or active ones, or staying visible
risks.mitigation: TC7 clears two completed todos amid an active one; TC6 checks hidden/visible transitions

acceptanceCriteria.text: Ticking a todo's checkbox marks it completed: its title is struck through and the 'items left' count goes down by one; unticking it removes the strike-through and restores the count.
The Active filter shows only uncompleted todos, Completed only completed ones, All every todo; the selected filter button is aria-pressed=true and the others false.
'Clear completed' is visible only while at least one todo is completed, and clicking it removes every completed todo and keeps the active ones.

testCases.title: ticking a todo strikes it through and decrements the items left count
testCases.expected: 'Buy milk' checkbox is checked and its title has text-decoration-line line-through; 'Walk dog' is not struck through; count reads '1 item left'

testCases.title: unticking a completed todo removes the strike-through and restores the count
steps: Tick 'Buy milk' and see '1 item left'
testCases.expected: Checkbox unchecked, title text-decoration-line none, count reads '2 items left'
testCases.rationale: Reversal is explicitly required and a common state bug

testCases.title: Active filter shows only uncompleted todos and is shown as pressed
testCases.expected: List items are exactly ['Buy milk', 'Pay rent']; Active aria-pressed=true, All and Completed false

testCases.title: Completed filter shows only completed todos and is shown as pressed
testCases.expected: List items are exactly ['Walk dog']; Completed aria-pressed=true, All and Active false

testCases.title: All filter shows every todo again and is shown as pressed
testCases.expected: List items are exactly ['Buy milk', 'Walk dog', 'Pay rent']; All aria-pressed=true, Active and Completed false
testCases.rationale: Returning to All must restore every todo

testCases.title: Clear completed is hidden until a todo is completed and hidden again when it is unticked
steps: Add 'Buy milk' and wait for it in the list
testCases.expected: Hidden with only active todos, visible once ticked, hidden again after unticking
testCases.rationale: The 'appears only while' half of AC3, including the negative state

testCases.title: Clear completed removes every completed todo and keeps active ones
testCases.expected: List items are exactly ['Walk dog']; count '1 item left'; Clear completed hidden
testCases.rationale: Removal of multiple completed todos without touching active ones

strategy.environmentNotes: Playwright's webServer in playwright.config.js starts `node server.js` on port 4173 (BASE_URL http://localhost:4173). Needs Chromium installed. No other services.

unticking a completed todo removes the strike-through and restores the count [chromium]

review.standard: Locators match full accessible names/text exactly (team rule)
review.summary: addTodos locates the title field with getByLabel('What needs doing?') and the submit button with getByRole('button', { name: 'Add' }), neither with exact: true, so both use case-insensitive substring matching (line 8 has the same problem).
review.failureScenario: If the page later gets a button whose name contains 'add', such as 'Add tag' or 'Address', getByRole('button', { name: 'Add' }) matches two elements and every test fails on a strict-mode violation. A second label containing 'what needs doing?' would break the field locator the same way. Add exact: true to both.

review.standard: Locators match full accessible names/text exactly (team rule)
review.summary: filter({ hasText: title }) at lines 9 and 18 matches list items by substring, so the toHaveCount(1) check in addTodos and the titleText item scope are not exact.
review.failureScenario: Suppose one title contains another, for example 'Buy milk' and 'Buy milk and eggs'. After the second add, filter({ hasText: 'Buy milk' }) matches 2 items, so toHaveCount(1) fails or proves the wrong item. In titleText the scope also matches both items, and getByText exact then finds only one span, but only by accident. Use hasText: new RegExp(`^${escaped}$`), or filter({ has: page.getByText(title, { exact: true }) }).

review.standard: Locators match full accessible names/text exactly (team rule)
review.summary: The list is located with getByRole('list', { name: 'Todos' }) without exact: true (also at line 9), so any list whose name contains 'todos' in any case would match.
review.failureScenario: If a second list is added, for example one named 'Archived todos', items(page) hits a strict-mode error, or the toHaveText list assertions are scoped ambiguously. Add exact: true.

review.standard: Locators match full accessible names/text exactly (team rule)
review.summary: The filter nav is located with getByRole('navigation', { name: 'Filter' }) without exact: true, while the button inside it is exact.
review.failureScenario: A second landmark whose name contains 'filter', such as 'Filter options' or 'Tag filter', makes filterButton ambiguous, and every filter and aria-pressed assertion fails on strict mode. Add exact: true.
